comparator.name: BSc in Business Administration (Bedrijfskunde)
comparator.sourceNotes: The July 2026 curriculum defines a 180-EC bachelor with a 60-EC first year, 60-EC second year and a 60-EC third year. For year 3, this pathway preserves 30 EC of genuine choice space as a 15-EC minor plus 15 EC of unnamed electives, then includes the compulsory Advanced Research Skills, Methods Master Classes and Cross Cultural Management and instantiates the Entrepreneurship for Growth track (17 EC). Entrepreneurship is selected under the neutral broad-identity rule because the programme explicitly makes entrepreneurship central across the first two years; the choice is not based on UCR fit. Current B3 rules checked on 20 October 2026 confirm that all 60 B1 EC must be completed before choice-space courses or track registration, that one complete track must be followed without mixing track modules, and that track allocation is capacity-constrained. Advanced Research Skills is 3 EC in block 3.3 in addition to the 30-EC choice block; the remaining core and track total 27 EC. No internship is compulsory in the selected minor-plus-electives pathway. Fresh 31 October 2026 verification confirms the current PDF and specific B3 guides over the generic page’s stale five-track phrase: three tracks, one complete 17-EC track, and 30-EC choice space plus 3-EC ARS in blocks 3.1–3.3 (33 EC), with 27 EC remaining. Repeated 7-EC project listings across two blocks count once. The source Ondernemingsrecht is translated as Corporate Law; commercial transaction law is not treated as its primary equivalent.

alternatives.label: Business, management & entrepreneurship
alternatives.concept: Business foundations, strategy and marketing connect with leadership, organisational psychology and international business. Accounting, financial markets and bank decisions, economics, empirical research and data analysis support the study of firms and management.
alternatives.labelReason: The selected programme spans business foundations, strategy, marketing, leadership, accounting, economics, international business and empirical methods. It does not claim a complete specialist finance or operations sequence.
progression: Current offerings, all earlier formal prerequisites and Year-1 PPD verified. Relevant economics, data and environmental foundations considered as soft advisory preferences, not new hard rules.

alternatives.label: Business, sustainability & responsible management
alternatives.concept: Business strategy, marketing, organisational behaviour and ethical leadership connect with climate, life-cycle assessment and circular resource use. Technical study of materials, farming and renewable energy supplies specific applications for evaluating sustainable business decisions.
alternatives.labelReason: The completed curriculum combines a substantial sustainability sequence with business strategy, marketing, leadership, economics, research and law, so the label names both business and sustainability rather than implying a pure sustainability programme.
alternatives.distinctness: Ten course differences from the closest option implement the independently evidenced sustainable-business direction through life-cycle assessment, climate, circular materials, renewable systems, farming/supply-chain applications, ethics and governance. Technical subjects provide bounded applications rather than substitutes for the disciplinary logistics sequence.
progression: Current offerings, all earlier formal prerequisites and Year-1 PPD verified. Relevant economics, data and environmental foundations considered as soft advisory preferences, not new hard rules.

alternatives.label: Finance, economics & business analytics
alternatives.concept: Financial statements, investment appraisal, securities and banking connect with economics, econometrics, probability and data methods. Programming and intelligent-agent decision theory provide complementary analytical tools; strategy, negotiation and international business connect the analysis to management.
alternatives.labelReason: Actual accounting/finance and sustained economics, statistics and data inquiry define the composition. No specialist portfolio-management, accountancy qualification or prescribed financial dataset is asserted.
alternatives.distinctness: Compared with the broad closest match and the sustainability route, this curriculum substitutes mathematics, programming, databases, optimisation, probability and additional economics/finance for much of the leadership, marketing, communication and sustainability content.
progression: Current offerings, all earlier formal prerequisites and Year-1 PPD verified. Relevant economics, data and environmental foundations considered as soft advisory preferences, not new hard rules.

routeSelection.basis: The generic Bedrijfskunde programme has three formal third-year tracks. Entrepreneurship is explicitly central across the first two years, including venture creation, innovation and growth, so Entrepreneurship for Growth most directly continues the programme-wide academic identity. The choice is independent of UCR fit.

selection.assessment: Two additional generator-backed directions are coherent and feasible after the closest match: Sustainable Business Strategies and Financial Analysis & Investment. Both produce curricula that are substantively distinct and exceed the 30-EC pairwise floor, so the maximum of three UCR alternatives is reached.

blocks: Product design develops innovation through customer needs, prototyping, costing and environmental assessment; it is narrower than a general Innovation Management course.

Emotion regulation, identity safety and inclusive leadership under pressure address an identifiable part of responsible organisational leadership. The full organisational-responsibility course is broader.
Market Research provides applied research design, data collection and analysis in a marketing setting; it does not reproduce the whole general management-research and literature-review course.

Econometrics provides causal/predictive regression and inference, using Stata. The RSM course also includes R, panel/time-series methods, introductory machine learning and optimisation; the courses are partial counterparts.
Mathematical Methods provides calculus and differential-equation techniques, including economic applications; the exact business-mathematics syllabus is not claimed to be identical.
No direct counterpart is established: AI-system planning does not by itself establish coverage of the business Decision Science syllabus.
The UCR course examines the business and governance implications of AI; it covers a particular technological domain rather than all of technology management.
Database Management Systems provides relational data structures and SQL; its technical scope is narrower than general business information management.

International Business & Governance develops an evidence-based market-entry strategy using country/business-function analysis. It supplies a specific business strategic-planning relationship, narrower than the RSM real-company strategic-advice project.
PPD provides first-year personal, collaborative and academic formation; its LAS setting differs from RSM business mentoring.
RSM Ondernemingsrecht concerns corporate law. Cross-border contracts, trade and arbitration do not by themselves establish a corporate-law subject sequence.
Country-entry/governance analysis provides institutional context, but does not establish the dedicated culture, leadership, communication and cross-cultural organisational-theory course.

notes.text: RSM Bedrijfskunde includes a dense compulsory sequence in business functions and a 7-EC track-linked bachelor project. The UCR programmes offer related business study but do not reproduce the complete HRM, management-accounting, operations, supply-chain, simulation or track/project structure. Technical sustainability and AI courses contribute specific applications. Partial row matches indicate related content, with differences in scope and credits.

audience.programmeDescription: Bedrijfskunde at Erasmus University Rotterdam examines how businesses operate and how managers address organisational problems. It combines business functions, entrepreneurship, economics, quantitative methods and research, followed by a specialised track and bachelor project.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Three UCR programmes approach business through broad management and entrepreneurship, sustainability and resource applications, or finance and analytics. They retain substantive business study, while RSM’s complete HRM, corporate-law, operations, supply-chain and management-accounting sequence and required 7-EC track project remain important differences.

curriculum.routeLabel: Dutch-language, full-time; Entrepreneurship for Growth track
curriculum.limitation: The selected 180-EC pathway includes a 15-EC minor, 15 EC of open electives and the 17-EC entrepreneurship track, including its 7-EC bachelor project. Track allocation depends on capacity. All 60 first-year EC are required before third-year choice-space or track registration; modules from different tracks are not combined.

componentNotes.b1-strategicplan: The UCR course develops an international market-entry strategy; the RSM component instead investigates a real company for strategic advice.
componentNotes.b2-law: Corporate law remains a gap. UCR transnational business law focuses on cross-border transactions and disputes.
componentNotes.b3-cross: The dedicated cross-cultural management component remains a gap.
componentNotes.b3-project: Required 7-EC entrepreneurship-track project with individual and group work. Optional UCR research is additional and unscheduled.
